topic: The Geometry of Light: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow
target_audience: High school geometry or physics students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Circles and Spheres
lecture_lines: A circle's area is pi times radius squared.
A sphere is points equidistant from center.
Parallel projection creates a flat shadow.
animations: Draw a circle with radius r using #FF5733 color.
Label the radius r clearly near the center.
Rotate the circle to form a sphere silhouette [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Highlight the surface area concept with a #3357FF glow [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: The Sphere Surface Area Formula
lecture_lines: Sphere surface area equals four pi r squared.
Imagine four circles covering the sphere's surface.
The coefficient four shows the ratio.
Total area is four times circle area.
animations: Start with a sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] of radius r in #FF5733.
Show the formula 4 * pi * r^2 in #FFD700.
Animate the growth of r and observe the area change of the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: The Relationship: Sphere Area vs. Projected Shadow
lecture_lines: Sphere surface area is four pi r squared.
Shadow area on flat plane is pi r squared.
The shadow is one-quarter of surface area.
This ratio holds from every angle.
animations: Show sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] in #FF5733 and its projection as a circle.
Highlight the circle area as pi * r^2 in #33FF57.
Show that 4 projected circles fit the sphere surface [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Animate the folding of circles onto the sphere surface [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Final equation 4 * pi * r^2 revealed in #FFD700 using the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Satellites use this ratio for heat.
Sunlight exposure depends on surface area.
Knowing area prevents overheating in space.
animations: Display a real-world object like an orange [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg] in #FF8C00.
Label the radius of the orange as r.
Summarize the surface area formula 4 * pi * r^2.
